title: They didn’t drop dead because of money.
paragraphs: They didn’t drop dead because of money.
They dropped… because of a lie no one could see.

Because what if the most dangerous sin in your life…
is the one you’ve learned to hide so well it looks like obedience?

You read the story of Ananias and Sapphira and think,
“That’s extreme.”

Because Acts 5 doesn’t start with judgment.
It starts with generosity. A church burning with purity. People giving freely, joyfully.

They sell land.
They bring an offering.
They lay it down at the apostles’ feet.
Peter confronts Ananias and says, “Why has Satan filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit…? You have not lied to man but to God” (Acts 5:3–4).
And God didn’t judge the amount.
Here’s the part we don’t like to admit:

We’ve mastered looking surrendered…
while secretly negotiating with sin.
We say, “God, You have all of me.”

But we keep the hidden folder.
The silent compromise.
The delayed obedience we call “waiting on the Lord.”

We lift our hands in worship…
while burying habits we refuse to confront.
What part of your life looks surrendered in public… but is withheld in private?
Have you confused appearing righteous… with actually being right with God?
Because Jesus warned about this kind of life.
He said in Luke 12:2, “Nothing is covered up that will not be revealed, or hidden that will not be known.”

Not the thoughts you replay at night.
Not the motives behind your “good works.”
Not the version of you no one else sees.
God is not exposed by your performance.
And here’s the mirror you can’t avoid:

You are not struggling because God is distant…
you are struggling because something is hidden.
This is where it gets uncomfortable.
Some of you don’t need more sermons.
Because partial obedience is still disobedience wrapped in religious language.
That’s the danger Ananias and Sapphira walked into.
This story is not just a warning.
It’s a revelation of how seriously God takes truth in His presence.
The One who judged deception in Acts 5—
Is the same God who made a way for sinners to be made clean.
And the weight of it… leads to death.
Romans 6:23 says, “The wages of sin is death…”
But the verse doesn’t end there.
“…but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.”
Christ was exposed on the cross.
For the hidden parts we hope no one finds out.
2 Corinthians 5:21 says, “God made Him who knew no sin to be sin for us…”
“So that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.”
You don’t have to pretend to be righteous.
Here’s the conviction line you need to hear:
God is not impressed by what you display—He is after what you surrender.
You are not called to manage sin quietly…
You are called to walk in the light boldly.
1 John 1:7 says, “If we walk in the light, as He is in the light… the blood of Jesus cleanses us from all sin.”
So why are you still hiding?
Grace is not an excuse to conceal sin.
Grace is the invitation to confront it—and be free.
Some scholars interpret the severity of Acts 5 as God establishing purity in the early church.
The same God who revealed sin publicly…
Bring the hidden into the light.
If this hit something deep in you… don’t ignore it.
You don’t have to stay stuck.
You don’t have to fake it anymore.
And next time, we’re going deeper into the sins that look holy… but quietly destroy the soul.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
